text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fire guts the first floor of Cabinet Office, the headquarters of government, destroying important documents, office furniture and equipment.

- President Frederick Chiluba asks the African Development Bank not to renew funding to Italian firm Alstadi Constructors, whom he says have done a bad job of rehabilitating one of the country's most important roads.
- Chairman of the defunct Meridien BIAO Bank, Andrew Sardanis, and four others appear in a Lusaka courtroom to answer 134 counts of receiving deposits when they knew the bank was collapsing.
- At least 34 people in the northern mining town of Kitwe are injured when a mini-bus and van collide.
- Over 1,000 cattle have died of tick-borne disease in the central district of Kabwe since January.
- The University of Zambia lecturers and researchers association calls for the resignation of the chancellor of the troubled institution, John Mwanakatwe.
- Energy minister Suresh Desai says the government will no longer influence the price of fuel.
